transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you into the clinic today?

Thank you. Well, I'm here because for months now, I've been seeing this pattern. My sister's appointments keep getting moved, bills show up wrong, people just happen to forget to call me back... and even when everyone around me says it's just administrative mistakes, I know what I'm seeing. I know they're keeping information from me and trying to push me out of decisions.
Have you ever heard voices, sounds, or whispering when no one was around?

No, no I haven't. I don't hear voices or whispering or anything like that. It's nothing like that. My hearing is fine. I just... I see what's actually happening right in front of me with the paperwork and the schedules.
Have you been diagnosed with any medical or neurological conditions?
No, no I haven't. I don't have any medical conditions... or neurological ones, either. My physical health is perfectly fine.

Looking back throughout your life, have you generally found it difficult to trust people and felt that others have hidden motives, even before these issues with your sister began?

No, not really. I've never had a problem trusting people before. I mean, I've supervised office staff for a long time, and you have to be able to trust people to do that job. I've always gotten along fine with everyone. It's really just... what's happening right now with my sister. Before all this started with her, I didn't go around thinking people had hidden motives.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a well-systematized, non-bizarre persecutory belief lasting for several months, centered on perceived deliberate administrative sabotage and concealment of information regarding her sister. Prominent auditory hallucinations, thought interference, and other Schneiderian first-rank symptoms of schizophrenia are absent. Furthermore, there is no lifelong pervasive pattern of mistrust or paranoia prior to the onset of these events, ruling out paranoid personality disorder.
